sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Madison County, KY?
sections.html:
Madison County splits the work across three offices in Richmond: the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) values the land and buildings, the Sheriff's Office bills and collects, and the County Clerk records deeds and takes over bills that go unpaid. Knowing which desk answers which question saves a lot of phone calls.

  • The PVA answers questions about assessed value, mailing address changes and exemptions. The Sheriff's Office lists the PVA at 859-623-5410.
  • The Sheriff's Office is at 135 W Irvine, Suite B01, Richmond, and takes payment online, in person or by mail, Monday through Friday from 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM. Call 859-623-1511. The office warns owners not to mail cash.
  • The County Clerk's Richmond Branch is at 321 N. Madison Ave. and handles recordings, with hours of 8 AM to 4:30 PM. A second branch on Chestnut Street in Berea covers vehicle and marriage license work.

The sheriff is the collector of state, county, school and special district property tax under KRS 134.119. The sheriff may also accept payment from another person on the owner's behalf.

sections.h2: What should a home seller know about Madison County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Madison County is the fast-growing university county in the central part of the state, directly south of Fayette County. It was established in 1785 from a portion of Lincoln County, Virginia, and is named for James Madison. The county seat and largest city is Richmond, and the only other city is Berea.

Two schools shape the housing market. Eastern Kentucky University sits in Richmond and Berea College sits in Berea, and the 2020 census counted 40.5 percent of occupied homes as renter-occupied. Interstate 75, U.S. 25, U.S. 421 and KY 52 run through the county.

The county covers 443 square miles, of which 437 are land. Daniel Boone built Fort Boonesborough here in 1775, and the site is now a state historic site. Unincorporated places such as Kingston, Waco, Speedwell, Bybee and Union City mean many sellers hold rural parcels outside either city. Ask the sheriff which taxing districts appear on your bill, since the districts on a bill depend on where the parcel sits.

Old farm tracts near the cities can look very different on paper from the house lots next to them. Kentucky values working farmland at its agricultural use value under Section 172A of the state constitution, so a seller with a farm should ask the PVA how each acre is classified before setting a list price.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Madison County housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimates show a county that is more expensive and more rental-heavy than most of Kentucky, with the median owner-occupied home valued at $232,000.

sections.h2: When are Madison County property taxes due, and what does a late payment cost?
sections.html:
Madison County bills follow the statewide calendar in KRS 134.015, and the dates printed on your bill control. The Sheriff's Office tells owners to rely on the payment periods shown on the current bill or in its online tax portal.

  • Pay in full by November 1 of the assessment year and take a 2 percent discount.
  • Pay November 2 through December 31 and owe the face amount.
  • Pay in January and add a 5 percent penalty.
  • Pay after January 31 and the penalty is 10 percent.

The Department of Revenue can swap in a later schedule when bills are delayed, with the discount lasting one month from the mailing date. A sheriff's collection fee is stacked on top once a bill is delinquent. That fee equals 10 percent of the tax plus 10 percent of the penalty under KRS 134.119(7).

A bill that is still open when the sheriff's window closes moves to the clerk as a certificate of delinquency, and the Department of Revenue's collection guide says interest of 1 percent per month starts to run then. The Madison County Clerk posts a 2025 delinquent county property tax list, updated August 31, 2026, along with a page for third-party purchasers.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Madison County assessment?
sections.html:
Start by asking the Madison County PVA for a conference, then go to the county board of assessment appeals if you still disagree. The sequence comes from KRS 133.120, which the General Assembly amended effective July 15, 2026.

  1. Request the conference before or during the tax roll inspection period. You may ask for it by telephone.
  2. Listen to how the PVA arrived at your value. The office must keep a written record of the meeting.
  3. File a letter or petition with the County Clerk no later than one workday after inspection ends. Give the parcel, your reasons and the fair cash value you believe is right.
  4. Bring proof to the hearing: sales of similar homes, a mortgage appraisal, insurance paperwork or construction cost. An appeal without reasonable information is denied.

Under KRS 133.030 the board convenes between 25 and 35 days after inspection closes and meets for at most five days a year unless the Department of Revenue allows more. You may record the hearing, and the board must inspect the parcel if you ask. Keep paying: an appeal never delays collection, and you owe tax on the value you claimed while the case is open.

sections.h2: Can Madison County homeowners claim the homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Yes, if you own and live in the house and are at least 65 or totally disabled under a federal or retirement-system program. For the 2025 and 2026 assessment years, the Kentucky Department of Revenue sets the exemption at $49,100.

Apply with the Madison County PVA, which the sheriff's office lists at 859-623-5410. On a home valued at the Census median of $232,000, the taxable amount would drop to $182,900. Age can be shown with a birth certificate, driver's license or passport. Disability claims generally renew every year, except for service-connected veterans and people ruled permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

The exemption belongs to the owner, not the house. When a Madison County homeowner sells, the buyer files a new application if eligible, and the seller should tell the PVA about the sale.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid tax when a Madison County house is sold?
sections.html:
The lien stays with the property until someone pays it. KRS 134.015(5) lets a delinquency lien last up to eleven years, whoever owns the parcel, so a title company will find it and require payoff.

The Madison County Attorney's Office assists the Department of Revenue with delinquent collection and sends letters that warn of foreclosure. Its delinquent tax page says an owner may qualify for an installment agreement on terms the County Attorney sets. If that agreement is made before the Clerk's sale and payments stay current, the underlying bills cannot be bought by investors. Questions go to 624-4777, extension 9.

Even when everything is current, the sheriff's guidance is that taxes are commonly prorated between buyer and seller at closing and the current owner must make sure the bill is paid. Review your closing statement line by line, and ask the sheriff for a balance before you list.

sections.h2: How are deeds recorded and taxed when selling in Madison County?
sections.html:
Deeds go to the Richmond Branch of the Madison County Clerk, and the clerk collects Kentucky's transfer tax before accepting the document. The tax is fifty cents for each $500 of value or fraction, charged to the grantor under KRS 142.050. A $232,000 sale would owe $232.

The clerk's office holds documents from 1786 forward and can be searched by a person's name only. Records from 1986 on are scanned and reachable in person or through the subscription service ECCLIX. E-recordings are processed each morning until about 9:30 to 10:00, and the recordings desk is at (859) 624-4703, extension 3. Sellers who worry about deed fraud can join the clerk's free DocAlert service, which sends a notice when any document is recorded under their name or property.

Transfers between spouses in a divorce, foreclosure sales, and deeds from parent to child for nominal consideration are exempt from the tax.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Madison County, Kentucky?
faqs.a: The Madison County Sheriff's Office collects it at 135 W Irvine, Suite B01 in Richmond. It accepts online, in-person and mailed payments, and its number is 859-623-1511. Ask the PVA, not the sheriff, about assessed value.

faqs.q: How much is the Madison County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 off the assessed value for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. You must be 65 or older or totally disabled, and you apply with the Madison County PVA.

faqs.q: Is there a discount for paying Madison County tax early?
faqs.a: Yes, 2 percent when the bill is paid in full by November 1 of the assessment year under the standard schedule. After December 31 the penalty is 5 percent in January and 10 percent afterward.

faqs.q: Can I stop investors from buying my Madison County delinquent tax bill?
faqs.a: Sometimes. The County Attorney's office may offer an installment agreement, and bills covered by a current agreement made before the Clerk's sale cannot be bought by investors.

faqs.q: Does a Madison County assessment appeal pause my tax bill?
faqs.a: No. KRS 133.120 requires you to pay on the value you claim while the appeal runs, and any added tax is billed later with interest if the board's value is higher.
